children: Shares of biopharma company Jazz Pharmaceuticals

jumped 2.5% in the afternoon session after the company announced positive Phase 3 HERIZON-GEA-01 trial results showing that Ziihera combined with chemotherapy achieved a statistically significant overall survival benefit in advanced gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma.

Per a company press release, the second interim top-line analysis demonstrated a clinically meaningful overall survival improvement for Ziihera (zanidatamab-hrii) plus chemotherapy compared to trastuzumab plus chemotherapy in first-line HER2-positive locally advanced or metastatic gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma. This outcome marks a second survival win for the therapy following its FDA approval. The positive Phase 3 data reinforces the drug's therapeutic potential against standard treatment options, strengthening investor optimism regarding the commercial outlook for the company's oncology portfolio.
The shares closed the day at $250.79, up 2.6% from the previous close.
What Is The Market Telling Us

Jazz Pharmaceuticals’s shares are not very volatile and have only had 6 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful, although it might not be something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

Jazz Pharmaceuticals is up 44.8% since the beginning of the year, and at $250.75 per share, it is trading close to its 52-week high of $261.62 from August 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Jazz Pharmaceuticals’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $1,904.
